title: Stand up Consumption Central
audience: FinOps, IT admins, platform owners, finance partners
summary: One Power BI report for Copilot credit consumption and cost across Cowork/Work IQ, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot and Azure AI Foundry. Bring whichever products you have; each leaves its pages empty if you skip it. Start on sample data in ~10 minutes.

paths.label: Local CSV
paths.tagline: ~10 min · Power BI Pro · no Fabric

paths.label: Fabric
paths.bestWhen: Refreshes weekly on its own, keeps history.

paths.label: Viva Direct
paths.bestWhen: Cowork data with no files at all.

roles.label: GitHub enterprise admin or billing manager
Application Administrator (to register an Entra app)

steps.title: See what you're building
steps.body: Fifteen pages: consumption, cost, optimisation and forecast per product, plus a combined overview. Two minutes here saves an hour later.

steps.title: Decide which products you're reporting on
steps.body: No product is required — one is enough. Tick the ones you have in the tailor bar above; the rest just leave their pages empty and the steps disappear from this guide.

steps.title: Try it on sample data first
steps.body: Run the Local CSV path against the bundled synthetic dataset covering all four products. Proves the numbers before you wire up a tenant — no permissions needed.
steps.verify: The report opens with every page populated from synthetic data.

steps.title: Turn on Viva identification
steps.body: Viva ships Copilot data de-identified (hashed PersonId). Cowork totals and cost are fine either way, but department / cost-centre / manager / per-person views need this on. Not retroactive.
steps.verify: After ~24h, a fresh export shows UserPrincipalName instead of a hash.
steps.pitfall: Not retroactive — only exports taken after the policy carry UPNs.

ifMissing.message: Turning identification on needs Global Administrator or AI Administrator, and you hold neither. Without it you still get Cowork totals and cost — just not department or per-person breakdowns.
ifMissing.emailSubject: 2-minute admin task: turn on Viva identification for Copilot cost reporting
ifMissing.emailBody:
Hi,

I'm standing up Copilot credit reporting and need identification turned on in Viva Insights so we can break spend down by department. Only a Global Admin or AI Admin can do it, ~2 minutes:

1. https://admin.cloud.microsoft/?#/viva/featureAccessManagement
2. Settings > Viva > Feature access management
3. Create a policy: App = Viva Insights, Feature = Identification, Access = On
4. Takes up to 24h; only affects exports taken after it's on.

This processes personal data, so please apply our normal privacy review.

Thanks!

steps.title: Build the Cowork credit query in Viva
steps.body: Viva Insights → Analysis → custom query with the Copilot credit metrics. For self-refreshing paths turn on Auto-refresh and copy the Partition + Query identifiers.
steps.verify: The query returns credit rows (and a UPN column if identification is on).
steps.pitfall: Leave the GitHub Copilot credit metric out — it makes the Cowork query fail in Viva.

ifMissing.message: Building a Viva query needs the Viva Insights Analyst role, assigned inside Viva (not Entra) so we can't auto-detect it. An admin assigns it.
ifMissing.emailSubject: Please assign me the Viva Insights Analyst role
ifMissing.emailBody:
Hi,

For Copilot cost reporting I need the Viva Insights Analyst role. Steps: https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/insights/advanced/setup-maint/assign-user-roles

Thanks!

steps.title: Export the Copilot Studio usage reports
steps.body: Power Platform admin center → Licensing → Copilot Studio → export the three reports (Tenant, Per-agent, Per-user). PPAC is download-only.
steps.verify: You have StudioTenantDaily / StudioPerAgent / StudioPerUser CSVs.

ifMissing.message: Exporting Studio usage needs the Power Platform Administrator role, which you don't hold.
ifMissing.emailSubject: Please export Copilot Studio usage (or grant me Power Platform Admin)
ifMissing.emailBody:
Hi,

For our Copilot cost report I need the three Copilot Studio usage exports from the Power Platform admin center (Licensing > Copilot Studio): Tenant, Per-agent and Per-user. Either export them for me, or grant me Power Platform Administrator so I can pull them myself.

Thanks!

steps.title: Get the GitHub Copilot AI usage report
steps.body: GitHub → your enterprise → Billing & Licensing → Usage → AI usage → email the report. For the Fabric path you can automate it with a classic PAT instead.
steps.verify: You receive the AI usage CSV by email (or the API notebook pulls it).
steps.pitfall: The billing endpoints need a CLASSIC PAT — fine-grained tokens are rejected.

ifMissing.message: The GitHub AI usage report needs an enterprise admin or billing manager on your GitHub enterprise — that's a GitHub role, not an Entra one, so we can't detect it here.
ifMissing.emailSubject: Need the GitHub Copilot AI usage report for cost reporting
ifMissing.emailBody:
Hi,

For our Copilot cost report I need the GitHub Copilot AI usage report. From GitHub > enterprise > Billing & Licensing > Usage > AI usage > Get usage report (up to 31 days) > Email me the report. If we want it automated, I'll need a classic PAT with read:enterprise or manage_billing:copilot.

Thanks!

steps.title: Set up Azure AI Foundry collection
steps.body: Azure spend + tokens come from Cost Management + Monitor. For the Fabric path this needs an Entra app registration, a Key Vault secret, and Cost Management Reader on the billing scope. For Local CSV you can just export from Cost Analysis.
steps.verify: Cost Analysis shows the Copilot / Foundry meters; the app can read them.
steps.pitfall: Fabric's getToken audiences don't include ARM — the notebook needs an explicit app secret from Key Vault, not a managed identity.

ifMissing.message: Automated Azure collection needs both the ability to register an Entra app (Application Administrator) and Cost Management Reader on the billing scope. If you can't get these, skip Azure — the Foundry page just stays empty (supported), or export Cost Analysis CSVs by hand for the Local CSV path.
ifMissing.emailSubject: Need an app registration + Cost Management Reader for Copilot Azure cost reporting
ifMissing.emailBody:
Hi,

To pull Azure AI Foundry / Copilot credit spend into our cost report (Fabric path) I need:
1. An Entra app registration with a client secret in Key Vault (Application Administrator can create it), and
2. Cost Management Reader on the billing account/subscription scope.

Setup detail: https://github.com/microsoft/ConsumptionCentral-for-Microsoft-Copilot/blob/main/docs/ADVANCED-SETUP.md#azure-ingestion-in-fabric

Thanks!

steps.title: Load it: drop files in a folder, open the template
steps.body: Put every export in one folder (names are auto-recognised), open Consumption Central - Local CSV.pbit, paste the folder into DataFolder, click Load.
steps.verify: Every product you loaded fills its pages.

steps.title: Create a Lakehouse
steps.body: Fabric portal → your workspace → New → Lakehouse. Everything below writes into this one. PPU alone is not Fabric capacity.
steps.verify: The Lakehouse exists and has a SQL analytics endpoint.

ifMissing.message: The Fabric path needs a workspace on Fabric capacity (F SKU or eligible trial). If you only have Power BI Pro, use the Local CSV or Power Automate path instead.
ifMissing.emailSubject: Need Fabric capacity for Copilot cost reporting
ifMissing.emailBody:
Hi,

The scheduled-refresh version of our Copilot cost report needs a Fabric-capacity workspace (F SKU or trial). Could we get one assigned, or should I use the non-Fabric path?

Thanks!

steps.title: Wire Viva in via Dataflow Gen2
steps.body: The preferred Cowork route, no notebook: a certified Dataflow Gen2 writes your Viva query straight into the Lakehouse table viva_credits_weekly on a schedule.
steps.verify: The table populates on the schedule you set (Tue ~8am PST works).
steps.pitfall: Leaving Query Name blank only works against a custom Analysis query, and you must also turn on Auto-refresh for the query itself.

steps.title: Import the ingestion notebooks
steps.body: From the repo's 2. Fabric/notebooks/, import only the ones for your products, set your Lakehouse as each notebook's default (Explorer pane → pin → star — there is no Lakehouse variable to edit), fill the top cell, run.
steps.verify: Each notebook writes its tables; the SQL endpoint shows them.
steps.pitfall: Notebooks target their ATTACHED default Lakehouse, not a variable. Azure & Studio-API notebooks need an explicit Key Vault secret — a managed identity is not enough.

steps.title: Open the Fabric template and schedule
steps.body: Copy the Lakehouse SQL endpoint, paste it + the Lakehouse name into Consumption Central - Fabric.pbit, Load. Then schedule ingestion BEFORE the semantic-model refresh, on success only.
steps.verify: Report refreshes from the Lakehouse on schedule.

steps.title: Open the Viva Direct template
steps.body: Paste the Partition + Query identifiers from your auto-refreshing Cowork query into Consumption Central - Viva Direct.pbit, Load. Cowork with no files at all; other products optional via a folder.
steps.verify: Cowork pages refresh straight from Viva.
steps.pitfall: (500) Internal Server Error = identifiers point at the multi-table Consumption Dashboard export, not a custom Analysis query.

steps.title: Deploy the Dataverse tables
steps.body: Run Deploy-DataverseSchema.py (dry-run first, then --execute) to create the 11 tables. Needs System Administrator on the Dataverse environment.
steps.verify: The 11 cc_ tables exist in your environment.

ifMissing.message: Creating the Dataverse tables needs System Administrator on the environment, which you don't hold.
ifMissing.emailSubject: Need System Admin on a Dataverse environment for Copilot cost reporting
ifMissing.emailBody:
Hi,

To stand up the Power Automate + Dataverse path for our Copilot cost report I need System Administrator on the target Dataverse environment so I can deploy 11 tables (a script does it, dry-run first). Could you grant that, or run the deploy for me?

Thanks!

steps.title: Import and run the flows
steps.body: Import the flow package, set the connection variables, run each Backfill once, then switch on the four daily flows. Only the four API-backed feeds automate; the rest load by hand.
steps.verify: Daily flows show green runs; Dataverse tables fill.
steps.pitfall: The Studio flows currently 403 even for a Global Admin — this path is in testing.

steps.title: Open the Power Automate + Dataverse template
steps.body: Fill DataverseServer / Database / Prefix in Consumption Central - Power Automate + Dataverse.pbit, Load, publish, schedule.
steps.verify: Report reads the Dataverse tables and refreshes on schedule.

steps.title: Add department breakdowns (optional)
steps.body: For department / cost-centre grouping beyond what Viva carries, an Entra org export helps. Reports Reader can pull it.
steps.verify: org_attributes / entra_org.csv joins to your consumption on UPN.

ifMissing.message: A directory export for richer org attributes needs Entra Reports Reader. It's optional — identified Viva data already carries department, so skip this unless you need extra attributes.
ifMissing.emailSubject: Need an Entra directory export (Reports Reader) for cost chargeback
ifMissing.emailBody:
Hi,

For department-level Copilot chargeback I'd like an Entra directory export (UPN + department + cost centre). Reports Reader can pull it. Could you help, or grant me the role?

Thanks!
